description: The plot illustrates how accuracy-related metrics vary as a function of initial confidence, showing three series with error bars. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.86 to 1.00 with tick labels at irregular but closely spaced values (e.g., 0.86, 0.88, 0.89, …, 1.00). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with major ticks at 0.2 intervals. A blue solid line with circular markers stays high across the range, starting near 0.93 at 0.86 and ending near 0.98 at 1.00, with values generally between about 0.95 and 1.00 and reaching around 1.00 near 0.97–0.99. An orange dashed line with diamond markers labeled “Δ Accuracy” decreases from about 0.28 at 0.86 to around 0.13 by 0.91, rises to about 0.20 at 0.92, then drops to its lowest region around 0.05–0.10 between roughly 0.94 and 0.99, and increases again to about 0.20 at 1.00. A green dash-dot line with square markers labeled “Initial Accuracy” increases from about 0.64 at 0.86 to around 0.84 at 0.91, dips to about 0.77 at 0.92, then rises to around 0.92–0.93 near 0.95–0.96, stays near 0.89–0.92 through about 0.99, and drops to roughly 0.77 at 1.00; all three series include vertical error bars at each x-value.
